Kenya response pillars

SSurveillance & dataAlert investigation, contact tracing, line-list quality and cross-border intelligence.
IIPC / case managementTriage, isolation, PPE, safe patient movement, WASH and safe dignified burial.
LLaboratorySpecimen referral, testing capacity, biosafety, QA and turnaround time.

Do not assume

Travel or geography alone does not establish Ebola risk. Review symptoms, timing, epidemiologic exposure and current Kenya MoH/WHO definitions together.

Malaria and other serious febrile illnesses remain important differentials. A positive malaria result, absence of bleeding, or prior prophylaxis does not by itself resolve an Ebola concern.

Response orientation

First 24 hoursFirst weekMaintain throughout deployment
Mission brief; MoH/KNPHI reporting line; security and movement plan; current case definition and alert pathway; PPE and exposure procedures.Map stakeholders and facilities; review alert/contact data flows; observe triage/IPC; identify training and supply gaps; agree corrective actions.Document capability gained, not only activities: training → competency → gap → corrective action → follow-up → sustained capability.

Field deployment

Field readiness checklist

Use this as a pre-departure and arrival prompt. Add institutional and mission-specific requirements after confirmation with the deployment lead.

Before travel

On arrival

Field kit prompts

  • Chargers, power banks, offline maps, printed source list and backup contact method.
  • Notebook or approved device; avoid copying names, phone numbers, passport numbers or patient histories into this tool.
  • Hand hygiene, PPE and decontamination supplies according to approved mission and facility procedures.

Daily close-out

  • What was observed? What was verified? What remains unknown?
  • Which gap was corrected, by whom, and by when?
  • What requires escalation to MoH/KNPHI, county leadership, WHO or CDC?

Escalate immediately

Occupational exposure, suspected case, unsafe patient movement, PPE breach, unavailable referral pathway or serious deterioration: notify the designated response lead and follow the current Kenya procedure without delay.
Surveillance / epidemiology

Investigation and data support

Use current Kenya MoH/KNPHI tools and definitions. This page is a field prompt, not a replacement case-investigation form.

Alert and case investigation prompts

  • Clinical syndrome and onset timeline.
  • Residence, work, care-seeking and healthcare-facility exposures.
  • Direct contact with blood/body fluids, sick persons, deceased persons or burial activities.
  • Travel/transit reconstruction, including land crossings and internal movement.
  • Healthcare, laboratory, cleaning, ambulance or PPE-breach exposure.
  • Household, social, animal and community context as indicated by the current protocol.
Do not use a hard-coded old country list, temperature threshold or exposure definition. Confirm the current Kenya MoH/WHO criteria.

Contact-tracing quality checks

  • Unique record ID rather than names in operational exports.
  • Exposure date(s), last exposure, follow-up schedule and outcome fields are complete.
  • Daily follow-up status is reconciled with county/team totals.
  • Contacts who cross borders have an agreed handover and privacy-preserving notification route.
  • Escalation criteria and referral instructions are visible to the team.

Data products deployers can support

Line-list review

Completeness, duplicates, missing dates, inconsistent classifications and timeliness.

Situation reporting

Reporting period, data cutoff, numerator/denominator and source owner clearly labeled.

Map products

Aggregate to county/facility catchment or corridor; never publish identifiable case/contact points.

IPC / case management

Safe care and patient movement prompts

Clinical and IPC actions must follow current Kenya MoH/KNPHI and WHO guidance, facility leadership and trained clinical teams.

Triage and isolation

  • Recognize alerts early and avoid unplanned movement through routine patient flow.
  • Use a designated assessment and referral pathway with advance communication.
  • Review signage, hand hygiene, PPE access, waste, cleaning and patient/family communication.

PPE and occupational safety

  • Use role-appropriate PPE and trained donning/doffing observers.
  • Keep clean/dirty zones and waste routes unambiguous.
  • Report and manage exposures through the approved occupational pathway.

WASH / safe dignified burial

  • Confirm water, hand hygiene, cleaning/disinfection and waste capacity.
  • Engage families, faith leaders and community representatives early.
  • Use current safe and dignified burial procedures; do not improvise.

Laboratory readiness

Specimen and testing pathway

Kenya MoH reported five BVD laboratory references in its 6 October update: NVRL, KEMRI laboratories in Nairobi and Kisumu, and mobile laboratories at Busia and Lwakhakha. Confirm current operational status, referral routes and acceptance criteria before use.

Kenya public-health laboratory network — reference locations

The Ministry of Health describes eight National Public Health Laboratory reference locations. The outbreak-specific sources also identify NVRL/KEMRI capacity in Nairobi and Kisumu and mobile laboratory references at Busia and Lwakhakha. Locations below are orientation references, not confirmation that a site is currently accepting specimens.

For a current referral route, specimen acceptance criteria, transport instructions and turnaround time, confirm directly through the designated Kenya MoH/KNPHI laboratory pathway.

Readiness questions

  • Which laboratories are currently designated and accepting specimens?
  • Who may collect, package, transport and receive specimens?
  • What are current turnaround times, result communication and escalation procedures?
  • Are PPE, triple packaging, labels, forms, reagents and cold-chain arrangements available?
  • How are invalid, rejected, delayed or damaged specimens managed?
  • What quality-assurance and biosafety checks are active?

Do not put in a public map

Specimen identifiers, patient names, phone numbers, exact household locations, contact addresses and detailed exposure histories belong only in an approved secure response system.

Training and mentoring

From training to sustained capability

Use training to produce observable competency, corrective action and follow-up—not only attendance counts.

Core training domains

  • Outbreak detection and investigation
  • Surveillance and contact tracing
  • IPC and PPE
  • Case management
  • Laboratory coordination
  • RCCE and infodemic management
  • Emergency operations coordination

Competency evidence

  • Observed donning/doffing with corrective feedback.
  • Correct alert interview and exposure timeline.
  • Specimen packaging and referral simulation.
  • Safe patient movement or ambulance handover drill.
  • Accurate situation-reporting calculation and cutoff labeling.

Training record fields

Date · county/facility · role · topic · trainer · attendance count · pre/post result · observed gap · corrective action · owner · follow-up date · sustained capability.

Use approved Kobo/XLSForm or training database

Source context

Kenya MoH reported 4,971 health workers trained at national and sub-national levels as of 6 October 2026. An earlier WHO Kenya weekly report described 108 trainers of trainees and refresher training in Busia, Turkana and Trans Nzoia; these figures are from different reporting periods and should not be combined.

Border health / points of entry

Cross-border readiness

Support Kenya-led surveillance and referral at airports, land borders and major corridors. Screening is not diagnosis; combine symptom review, timing, exposure and current criteria.

Priority reference points

  • Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (Nairobi)
  • Busia / Malaba corridor
  • Lwakhakha border point
  • Other POEs identified by Kenya MoH/KNPHI and county teams

Operational status, staffing, screening arrangements and referral capability must be verified locally.

POE assessment prompts

  • Clear alert-to-referral workflow and receiving facility communication.
  • Private assessment space, hand hygiene and PPE access.
  • Trained staff, supervision and shift coverage.
  • Transport/ambulance availability and contingency plan.
  • Traveler information, rumor management and disability/language access.

Movement intelligence

  • Land and air routes, transit hubs and seasonal movement.
  • Referral and notification arrangements across counties and borders.
  • Aggregate corridor data only; no public mapping of individual travelers or contacts.

Field communication

  • Use trusted Kenya MoH and county voices for public messaging.
  • Keep preparedness, suspected cases and confirmed cases clearly distinguished.
  • Track rumors and questions; do not amplify unverified claims.
  • Use English or Kiswahili materials approved for the audience and setting.

Update procedure

  1. Obtain the newest Kenya MoH/county and WHO report.
  2. Record report number, publication date and data cutoff.
  3. Update situation figures only from the same reporting period; label older context.
  4. Update structured arrays in the script: APP_VERSION, DATA_UPDATED, responseHubs, pointsOfEntry, laboratoryReferences, regionalContext, resources.
  5. Add a changelog entry and verify map popups, links, mobile layout and source credits.
